text:
olga: Quick check-in on side-channel CA rotation + authZ for the private CP handoff. exploring two patterns: 1) central sidecar/proxy that terminates tenant certs and does authz, 2) per-tenant agent with local CA and mTLS to controlplane. want tradeoffs + rollout concerns. thoughts?

sam: +1 we need to settle blast radius and trust propagation. do we want a single root CA or intermediate per-tenant?

pj: single root simplifies ops but increases blast radius. intermediate CA per-tenant gives isolation but is more complex for rotation.

mike: operationally, per-tenant intermediate that we sign from a central root seems like the sweet spot. can revoke one tenant without tearing down others.

olga: agree. also thinking about handoff: agent bootstrap vs sidecar handshake. agent can hold long-lived certs rotated by KMS, sidecar does ephemeral tokens and proxies.

tess: agent wins for offline/on-prem cases. sidecar better for hosted where we can centrally scale and observe.

sam: another piece is authZ model. if sidecar does RBAC decisions, we need to push policies into proxy and keep them synced. agent could enforce locally with a smaller policy surface.

pj: policy drift is scary. sync protocol has to be push-based and versioned. ideally include a policy hash in the handshake so controlplane can detect mismatches.

olga: sketch of possible handshake (high-level):
```
1) agent/sidecar connects to CP with TLS using intermediate cert.
2) CP returns policy-hash + allowed routes.
3) client performs authZ check via local policy cache; if mismatch, pull policy and re-evaluate.
4) periodic cert rotation via CA endpoint, cert TTL short for sidecars, longer for agents.
```

mike: note: short TTL implies frequent rotation load. we need an autoscaling plan for CA signing pods or a signing queue.

infra-bot: INFO: cert-rotation job queued for tenant-42 at 1718462800

pj: also consider CRL vs OCSP for revocation. CRL is heavy, OCSP gives realtime but we need highly available responder.

tess: OCSP stapling at the sidecar could help reduce latency. but that couples proxy and CA responder logic.

sam: what about zero-trust pattern where CP never accepts client certs directly, instead client mTLS to a regional relay that vends short-lived bearer tokens to reach CP? reduces CP attack surface.

olga: that would be our 'regional relay + token vending' option. pro: CP sees bearer tokens only. con: increases hop count and token management complexity.

mike: latency-sensitive paths (inference control signals) might suffer with extra hops. we can mark them as bypass routes for dedicated tenants.

pj: rollout plan suggestion:
- phase 1: implement intermediate CA issuance + per-tenant intermediates, agent optional for on-prem.
- phase 2: add policy-hash in handshake + push-based sync.
- phase 3: experiment with regional relay + token vending for hosted-only tenants.

olga: @sam @mike @pj can we own spikes: pj on CA infra + revocation, sam on policy sync semantics, mike on latency/relay perf? aiming for RFC follow-up in 2 weeks. :thumbsup:

sam: taking policy sync spike. will prototype a v1 push endpoint and a simple policy-hash compare. ETA 10 days.

pj: taking CA infra. will assess OCSP vs CRL, signing autoscale, HSM flow. ETA 14 days.

mike: I'll do relay perf benchmarks and a micro-proxy latency test. ETA 7 days.

deploy-bot: ACTION: created tasks: CA-spike(#3421) assigned to pj, policy-sync(#3422) assigned to sam, relay-perf(#3423) assigned to mike

olga: awesome. last note: document cheat-sheet of failure modes we care about (revocation, policy drift, CA compromise, key sync break). put that in the RFC so rollbacks are clear.

tess: will add failure-mode appendix to RFC draft and a short runbook for on-prem customers.

olga: thanks everyone. will draft follow-up RFC and link spikes. will ping in ~48h for initial sync. :wave:
